acceptance.criterion: byte identity, unchanged from the predecessor
greenConditions: the two replicas' kernel files are byte-identical
the two replicas' initrd files are byte-identical
the two replicas' root disk files are byte-identical
no timestamp anywhere in the image is a wall-clock value
loader provenance lies entirely inside the frozen closure on both replicas
frozen e2fsck -f -n exits 0 on both replicas

onGreen.mustRecord: that the digest is not one replica chosen over the other, but the single value both replicas independently converged on

timestampRule.rule: Every time field in the produced image is either the canonical source epoch or the ext4 writer time. Any third value is a reject, and any value large enough to be a plausible clock reading is definitionally a wall clock.
timestampRule.why: Stated as a closed set rather than as 'differs from expected', because a closed set cannot be widened after the fact to admit what was produced.

argvNotes.-f: force a full check. Without it e2fsck sees a clean superblock and exits 0 without reading the filesystem, and a pass that checked nothing is close enough to not running to be worthless.
argvNotes.-n: answer no to every question: the filesystem is opened read-only and nothing is written

binary.firstPinnedHereBecause: mke2fs and debugfs already carry digests in the plan module; e2fsck carries none anywhere, so this is a first pin rather than a copy of one.
binary.name: e2fsck

rejected.1: errors corrected -- impossible under -n, so its appearance means the contract was not honoured
rejected.128: shared library error, which would also mean the loader closure is wrong
rejected.4: errors left uncorrected: the filesystem is not clean

e2fsckContract.runOn: the produced image, in the job that produced it, before any comparison
e2fsckContract.why: The predecessor recorded that no filesystem check was run. Byte identity says two images agree; it does not say either one is a well-formed filesystem.

digestsAreNotRestatedHere.exception: e2fsck, pinned below because no existing record pins it
digestsAreNotRestatedHere.why: The pinned packages already carry these bytes. A second copy of a sealed fact can drift from it silently, so the expected digests are derived from the frozen packages at verification time rather than typed into this record.

emitDoNotRecompute.note: The value already exists at run time and is thrown away. The successor records that value rather than adding a second computation that could disagree with the one that actually fed the loader.

hardStopConditions: any resolved path outside the frozen extraction tree
any runner default library mixed into the resolved set
any resolved file whose bytes do not come from the frozen provider package
any required library missing from the emitted evidence
the two replicas' loader evidence differing in any field
requiredFields: absolute path of the dynamic loader actually invoked
absolute path of every shared library the frozen invocation points the loader at
sha256 of each of those real files as they exist on the runner
the frozen package each file is bound to
loaderEvidenceContract.why: The predecessor left 'loader-resolves-only-frozen-libraries' unsettled, because the executor computed the resolved library set and then discarded it. A run whose library provenance is not written down cannot be audited after the fact.

preRegistration.amendForbiddenReason: A pre-registration that can be rewritten after seeing the outcome is not a pre-registration. Follow-up implementation commits may be added to the same branch; this commit's bytes must stay as pushed.
preRegistration.purpose: Freeze the acceptance criteria, the fixed-time design, the loader evidence contract and the read-only filesystem check before any production code is changed, so a later result cannot be judged against a bar written after it.

predecessor.relationship: This record removes the cause that record identified. It does not revise, soften or supersede that record's failure verdict, which stands as written.

networkAllowed: payload acquisition from the Ubuntu snapshot the existing workflow already pins
GitHub Actions artifact upload and download
git push, pull request and CI checks
perReplicaReport: evidence that the fixed writer time was applied
loader actual paths and sha256 values
frozen e2fsck -f -n exit code and verdict

retryPolicy.onMismatch: HARD STOP; report; do not produce a third image
retryPolicy.rerunAllowedOnlyWhen: CI infrastructure failed before any artifact was created
retryPolicy.rerunForbiddenWhen: outputs were created and then did not match
retryPolicy.why: Re-rolling until two images agree measures patience, not determinism, and the first mismatch is the finding.

canonicalSourceEpoch.role: the logical timestamp every staged entry carries into the image; the historical record and the input's own meaning

debugfsMustNotBecomeAWriter.why: Stamping the image after the fact would produce a filesystem whose bytes no single tool accounts for, and would move the writer role to an inspector that v1 sealed read-only.

ext4WriterTime.reason: In this build of libext2fs, 0 is the unset sentinel: fs->now == 0 means 'nobody pinned a time', and every stamping site falls back to time(). 1 is the smallest value that is both non-zero and fixed, so it is the smallest change that makes the pin take effect at all.
ext4WriterTime.role: the value actually handed to the frozen e2fsprogs, which is a separate fact from what the staged inputs mean

forbiddenSubstitutions.why: this build reads no such variable; setting it would look like a fix and do nothing
a clock read at build time is exactly the non-determinism being removed
a number chosen for how it reads is a fact nobody can re-derive later
the sentinel; already falsified by the predecessor record

mechanicalPreVerification.answer: It reaches both, and it reaches every field that differed between the two replicas. Each stamping site loads fs->now from offset 0xb8 and branches on zero; the non-zero path stores that value directly, and time() is reached only through the zero branch.

coverage.claimLimit: This says a fixed non-zero value reaches every field that moved. It does not say the produced images will be identical; only a produced pair says that.

mechanicalPreVerification.digestsAreNotCopiedHere: These are the same two binaries the predecessor record pins by digest, and that record is bound above by path and sha256. Restating the hex here would create a second copy that can drift from the first without saying so.
mechanicalPreVerification.method: static disassembly of the exact frozen binaries with /usr/bin/objdump; nothing was executed to establish it
mechanicalPreVerification.performedBefore: any production change, any build, any result
mechanicalPreVerification.question: Does a non-zero E2FSPROGS_FAKE_TIME actually reach the superblock and the inodes mke2fs creates, or only the superblock?

sites.note: strtoul("1") is 1, so the successor value lands in fs->now as 1

sites.fallback: 0x2d3f8 bl time@plt, reached only when fs->now == 0
sites.instruction: ldr x0, [x25, #0xb8] -> 0x2cd2c cbz x0, 0x2d3f8 -> 0x2cd3c str w0, [x21, #0x40]

sites.fallback: 0x13aac bl time@plt then 0x13ab8 str w0, [x20, #0x30], reached only when fs->now == 0

sites.note: guarded by 0x30504 cbnz: written only where the field is still zero
reached only for inodes larger than 128 bytes (0x30524 cmp w22, #0x80; 0x30528 b.eq skips it). This image uses 256-byte inodes, so it applies.

sites.fallback: 0x81a8 mov x0, #0 / bl time@plt, reached only when fs->now == 0
sites.instruction: ldr x0, [x25, #0xb8] -> 0x7b24 cbz x0, 0x81a8 -> 0x7b4c stp w0, w0, [sp, #0xe0] -> 0x7b50 str w0, [sp, #0xe8]
sites.note: three consecutive 32-bit time slots filled from the same value

sites.instruction: mov x0, #0 -> 0x305d0 bl time@plt -> 0x305d4 mov w21, w0
sites.note: the only way a clock enters this function, and the zero sentinel is its only door

time.twoDistinctValuesOnPurpose: The staged inputs carry a logical epoch; the filesystem writer needs a clock. They were the same number before, and that is how a sentinel swallowed one of them unnoticed. They are separate fields now so neither can hide inside the other.
